content.tex: A INVESTIGATION (QUESTIONS 1 TO 4)
AREAS OF POLYGONS INSIDE AND OUTSIDE A CIRCLE (30 marks)
You are advised to spend no more than 50 minutes on this part.
This investigation looks at the areas of polygons drawn inside and outside a circle of radius 10cm.
An inscribed polygon is a polygon in which all the vertices lie on a circle. This is an inscribed square.
A circumscribed polygon is a polygon in which each side is a tangent to a circle. This is a circumscribed square.
You may find some of these formulas useful.
Area, A, of circle, radius \(r\) A \(= \pi r^{2}\)
Area, A, of triangle, base \(b\) , height \(h\) A \(= \frac{1}{2}bh\)
In a right-angled triangle,
\(\sin \theta = \frac{opposite}{hypotenuse}\) ,
\(\cos \theta = \frac{adjacent}{hypotenuse}\) ,
\(\tan \theta = \frac{opposite}{adjacent}\) .
